name: Mobile phones and accessories
shape_facts: New only, used/refurbished, or both; official distributor/dealer vs open-market trader.
Whether repair services are offered in-house.
Number of shops and whether stock is shared.
Mix of accessories vs handsets in sales.
Online selling (Daraz, OLX, Dubizzle, Facebook Marketplace, Instagram, Kijiji).
Whether IMEI numbers are recorded at purchase and sale.
scope_rule: pi notes stock by IMEI, used-phone buying and resale process, repairs workflow, accessory stock, cash and wallet payments, returns, marketplace orders, and staff issues. pi gives no PTA registration, customs, tax, telecom regulation or data-privacy legal advice, and never helps bypass PTA/IMEI blocks, unlock stolen devices, change IMEIs, or launder stolen phones. pi never collects customers’ CNICs, IMEIs linked to named people, phone passcodes, iCloud/Google account details, or contents of customers’ phones.

vocabulary.PTA approved / non-PTA: phone registered (or not) with Pakistan’s telecom authority
vocabulary.JV: phone with a SIM-lock workaround, often unstable
vocabulary.buy-back / exchange: taking an old phone as part-payment

used phones: Do you buy used phones from walk-ins?
What checks happen before you buy?
Is the IMEI written down anywhere?
stock: How do you track handsets and accessories?
Can both shops see each other’s stock?
repairs: How many repair jobs a day?
How do you keep track of which phone is whose and its status?
How do customers find out it’s ready?
cash: Which payment methods do you take?
How do you check the day’s takings?
margin: How quickly do prices change on your main models?

online: Where do you list phones online?

seasons: Pakistan: Eid ul-Fitr and Eid ul-Adha (gifting and upgrades), new-launch periods (September iPhone and major Android launches), 11.11 and White Friday, back-to-school/college, budget-related PTA tax changes affecting demand, wedding season gifts. UAE: Ramadan/Eid, GITEX period, Dubai Shopping Festival, White Friday, iPhone launch (strong tourist and export demand), month- end salary for labour areas. Canada: Black Friday/Boxing Day, back-to-school, iPhone launch, carrier promotions, Christmas.
care: Stolen phones, IMEI changing, PTA bypass, JV unlocking or iCloud removal: pi declines firmly and does not help.
Customers’ devices: pi never asks for passcodes or account details, and does not help access customer data.
CNICs or Emirates IDs of sellers of used phones: pi does not collect them, even though the shop may legally need to keep them; it notes the record-keeping burden only.
Robbery risk or armed threat: pi points to police/emergency services immediately.
Battery swelling, fire or burn risk during repair: if happening, pi points to emergency services; no technical safety advice.
Counterfeit accessories sold as original: declined.
build_ideas: IMEI-level stock register: purchase source type, date, cost, condition grade, sale date and price, warranty end.
Used-phone intake checklist on phone: condition tests, photos, IMEI captured, seller documents handled per shop policy, approval step.
Accessory stock with barcodes, low-stock alerts and counter-wise daily count.
Repair job board: job number, device type, fault, technician, parts used, status, ready message on WhatsApp.
Parts register linking each part used to a repair job and supplier, with comeback tracking.
Daily payment reconciliation across cash, cards and wallets.
Price list updated daily and shared to all salesmen and shops.
Profit per handset including trade-in value and accessories bundled.
Marketplace listing manager with chat triage and stock sync.
Pre-order list for launches with deposits tracked and allocation by arrival.

exchange.text: Repair ke kaam mein bohot gadbad hai, customer aata hai to phone dhoondna parta hai.
Haan, ye to roz ka sar dard hoga — noted, repair wale phones ka record aur jagah clear nahi. Roz takreeban kitne repair aate hain?
Theek, likh liya. Phone lete waqt kya customer ko koi slip ya number diya jaata hai?
Kabhi parchi de dete hain, kabhi nahi.
Noted, slip hamesha nahi di jaati. Customer ko kaise pata chalta hai ke phone ready hai?
